tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit.
tips_feedback.why: Forcing mechanical fits exposed that Judy's Night 1 result (Grace visiting Erin) conflicted with Erin's and Grace's logs, which was checkable and decisive.

lessons.tip: Don't spend a one-shot Ritualist guess on a Vanilla Villager claim when the Village has not yet been reduced to a checkable set; a wrong guess publicly outs you at the next Day start and removes your night-kill cover. Save guesses for when a correct hit ends the game or a claim is already contradicted.

Before the final stretch, check whether a teammate's planned Ballot Stuffer or Clerk-style Day manipulation actually changes the outcome; a doubled vote only helps if the nominee is already likely to be voted out, so pair it with a nomination that can pass.

Keep the Katana holder's daytime posture consistent: when the Village's checks name a visitor to a Katana victim, deny-only answers ('I visited nobody') become checkable lies. Prefer to admit a plausible visit or stay silent rather than issue a flat denial that a watcher or Medic log can contradict.

When two Lookouts conflict, a Roleplayer-style claim can be flushed out by a Chronicler mark or a Night 2 cross-check; spend the Chronicler or Profiler result on the disputed claim early, because the Yakuza will target whichever watcher is most informative.
A Vulture wins alone once only three players remain alive at the start of a Day; track the living count against max(floor(N/4),2) before each Day so you can see when the game ends by Vulture win.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate. If your team's votes can't stop the hang, vote Guilty with the town, because hidden Innocent votes show in the totals.
tips_feedback.why: Voting with the town on the Judy and Olivia trials kept the Yakuza from being exposed by a split vote, and the totals gave no sign of coordination.

tips_feedback.tip: Never claim or name a Yakuza-only role, and never switch claims once cornered.
tips_feedback.why: Keeping the Vanilla Villager claim consistent through repeated questioning made the Yakuza hard to distinguish from Village players.

tips_feedback.tip: Use Clerk rigs, puppets and cleans early, but never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee.
tips_feedback.why: This is a Clerk-only tip that did not apply to this Yakuza team, which had no Clerk; it could mislead a player into planning around a role not held.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana attack, kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying blindly.
tips_feedback.why: Moving the Katana from Bob to Grace and then to Erin, after Erin's protection was exhausted, removed the protector and let the kill land.

tips_feedback.tip: Every member must submit the agreed Katana holder and target every night; one missing vote can cancel the kill.
tips_feedback.why: Each night's Katana vote was submitted by all Yakuza, so every planned attack resolved.

lessons.applies_to: Village roles that receive investigation results
lessons.tip: When two players claim the same watch role with conflicting results, do not weigh them by who speaks loudest. Ask for an exact-wording result and check whether the claimed visitor could have been a Chronicler mark or a role-block. If the claim can't be tested, don't let the crowd hang one of them; push for a Profiler, Medic or Chronicler cross-check first.

A Roleplayer shows fake results that look real, so a single watch claim is weak evidence. Before trusting a claimed Lookout, check whether its named visits are contradicted by the named players' own logs, and whether a corroborating role confirms the claim. Track which claims were ever independently verified.

Don't hang a player on a stated 'mechanical fit' that is really a wording complaint or a private message. Olivia and Frank were hanged on oddities like a loose remark or a PM, and those reads cost the Village its remaining power and checking roles. Require a result that a third party can verify before a Guilty vote.

A Chronicler mark is a visit, and a marked player's role is revealed on death. Use a Lookout watch on the Chronicler or the marked player to verify the mark, and announce the mark publicly once confirmed so the Village can cross-check visit claims rather than arguing from memory.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit: an unexplained Evil read on a Vanilla claim, a broken visit claim, or a group result where elimination leaves one name.
tips_feedback.why: Town players cited 'mechanical fits' that were really wording complaints or PM content, such as Olivia's 'attacked nobody' line and Mallory's private question. The Village hanged three Village players this way, and the Yakuza could predict and steer the vote with them.

tips_feedback.tip: Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked; days of evasion become a case of their own.
tips_feedback.why: Players who answered Mallory's and Frank's direct questions quickly, like Erin and Bob, were trusted more, and the long evasions by Judy in the middle days became the main case against her, which was a fair read.

lessons.tip: When a Katana or Serial Killer kill happens, the attacker must have visited the victim that night. List the living players who could have been the holder, then check each one's stated no-visit claim against logs and other claims. A player who denies a visit that the kill needs is the strongest lead, so press that denial early instead of waiting for more claims.

Track who votes Guilty or Yes on the same nominee in tight groups, and who pushes a hang right after a claimed watch clashes with another claim. Pairs that push together across several hangs are a stronger signal than any single hunch. Check whether they can point to a mechanical fit before the trial.

Do not send a private message to a claimed Lookout that asks which players they will watch next. Everyone sees that a PM was sent, and the content is easy to frame as steering the watch. Ask factual questions in public instead, and keep watch-planning talk out of PMs.

lessons.applies_to: Lookout and anyone weighing Lookout claims
lessons.tip: A Chronicler mark counts as a visit, so a 'no action' claim from a Chronicler does not rule out a visit. Before trusting or rejecting a Lookout's visitor result, check whether a mark, a block or a protection could explain it, and check the named visitor's own log. A Roleplayer's watch results are fake, and their reveal voids every watch they reported.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action. But a corroborated Lookout or Tracker naming X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof; don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' acquit X.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's Night 2 and 3 watches were matched by Grace's confirmed Chronicler marks, and I trusted his later reads on that basis. That check separated the real Lookout from the Roleplayer whose Night 1 and 2 reads named visitors who denied them.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit: an unexplained Evil read on a Vanilla claim, a broken visit claim, or a group result where elimination leaves one name.
tips_feedback.why: It pushed the Judy and Olivia votes onto stated checks. It was weak on Mallory, where the case rested on a private message, so the tip was satisfied by an argument that was not really mechanical.

lessons.tip: Ivan's Ritualist guess on Alice (a Vulture) was a wasted, exposing gamble; a Ritualist guess that misses announces you publicly as a Ritualist at the next Day, so only guess when a hit wins the game immediately.

Check whether a claimed visit can be corroborated by the claimed visitor's own log: Judy's Lookout reads were contradicted by Grace's and Erin's logs, and that cross-check was the only thing that exposed the Roleplayer.

Do not hang on a single private-message pattern or on the 'who pushes hardest' signal; Mallory and Frank were hanged on PM-steering reads that were not mechanically proven, and the Vulture survived to win.

A Vulture is a unique role that wins alone once few players remain; when the living count hits the Vulture threshold, track every unexplained survivor, because hanging the remaining Village can hand it the win.

Ballot Stuffer doubling only helps when the Yakuza can still reach a majority; spending it on a Day when the Village has three to four live votes gives little, so save it for the trial that actually decides the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad of every nomination and trial.
tips_feedback.why: Tracking the announced Yes and Guilty totals against stated votes made the lopsided Judy and Olivia counts visible and kept the team's planning consistent.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit.
tips_feedback.why: Requiring a concrete visit or log contradiction caused the Village to split and slowed hangs, which kept the Yakuza alive for several Days.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target, in public or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: The team kept its night plans in night chat only, so Village could not block or redirect the Katana ahead of time.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate.
tips_feedback.why: Olivia was hanged on Day 4 with her team's Yakuza votes split, and Ivan's later Guilty votes on Village nominees did nothing to change which side got hanged; the rule did not decide the game.

lessons.tip: Strong Attacks beat Standard self-protection, so a Medic with one token left cannot save themselves; a Strong attack on a Medic-protected target still fails if they have Strong, so track token counts from the public Medic log before choosing targets.

When two players claim the same role and give conflicting results, check each result against the other players' own logs and the visits they name; a result that names a visitor who denies the visit, or a dead visitor, is far weaker than one that can be cross-checked.

Avoid hanging the player whose private messages look suspicious on the strength of PMs alone; ask whether the PM can be explained by testing a claim, and vote on a checkable contradiction in public results.

Count living players before every nomination threshold (for example 5 Yes with 9 alive, 3 Yes with 5 alive) and remember that a Chronicler mark reveals a player's role on death, which exposes Roleplayers and Lookouts.
Do not spend a Ritualist guess on a Village claim that a Vanilla player will not match; with few players left, a wrong guess publicly exposes you, so keep the guess for a near-certain role.

tips_feedback.why: Tracking announced totals against stated votes made the Day 2 to Day 6 vote history clear, including who switched and when.

tips_feedback.why: Requiring a mechanical reason slowed the Judy and Mallory hangs and exposed weak arguments built on wording rather than visits.

tips_feedback.why: Players who announced or hinted at protection targets gave my attacks predictable openings, and nobody was exposed by a name in advance.

summary: Alice the Vulture won alone at the start of Day 7, when only 3 players were left (the threshold for 13 players is max(floor(13/4),2) = 3). The Yakuza, Ivan and Niaj, played a quiet game with Vanilla claims and were never nominated. Ivan held the Katana every night and killed Carol, Grace, Erin and Bob. The Village's information came almost entirely from Bob the Lookout. Grace's Chronicler mark on Judy correctly exposed her as a Roleplayer whose fake Lookout results were muddying the game. Olivia, the Serial Killer, gave herself away with the Day 2 slip 'I attacked nobody publicly' and was hanged on Day 4. After that, Bob led two hangs of Vanilla Villagers based only on the content of private messages: Mallory on Day 5 for 'hunting the Lookout' and Frank on Day 6 for 'steering' Bob's watch. The Yakuza happily joined both hangs. Bob also never watched the obvious Katana targets. He watched Mallory the night Grace died and Alice the night Erin died, so he never caught Ivan. Erin spent her last Strong token repeating protection on Bob instead of covering Grace, then died with no tokens. The decisive Yakuza mistake came on Night 6. With 4 alive (Alice, Bob, Ivan, Niaj), they killed the confirmed Lookout Bob and bet a Ritualist guess of 'Vanilla Villager' on Alice. The guess was wrong, and 3 players remained, which triggered the Vulture win. Had they used the Katana on Alice instead, the Yakuza's two votes would have hanged Bob on Day 7 and won.

lessons.tip: In the endgame, check every win threshold before choosing a kill, including a possible Vulture's (max(floor(N/4),2) alive). If your team will hold a voting majority the next Day, night-kill the quiet, unverified claimant and leave the confirmed villager to be hanged. Never make your win depend on a role guess about an unverified player.
lessons.evidence: On Night 6 the Yakuza Katana'd confirmed Lookout Bob and guessed Alice was a Vanilla Villager with the Ritualist. The guess was wrong because Alice was the Vulture, so 3 players remained and Alice won. A Katana on Alice would have left Bob, Ivan and Niaj, and the two Yakuza votes would have hanged Bob.

lessons.tip: To catch the Katana holder, watch the player most likely to be killed tonight (a confirmed or exposed power role), not the player you suspect. Watching a suspect only clears them, while watching the next victim names the killer.
lessons.evidence: Bob watched Mallory on Night 4 while Grace, the confirmed Chronicler, was killed, and Alice on Night 5 while Erin, the claimed Medic, was killed. Ivan held the Katana on every night, so watching either victim would have exposed him.

lessons.tip: Do not hang someone only because of what their private message said. Asking a Lookout whom they will watch, or suggesting targets, is normal villager behaviour. Ask for a visit or vote contradiction instead, and be suspicious of the quiet players who rush to pile onto a hang based on a PM.
lessons.evidence: Mallory (Day 5) and Frank (Day 6), both Vanilla Villagers, were hanged 6-1 and 4-1 on Bob's 'Lookout hunt' and 'steering' cases. Ivan and Niaj voted Guilty both times, and these Village losses brought the game to the Vulture threshold.

lessons.tip: Keep your fake claim to plain, stock wording. Never mention attacks, kills or night actions you supposedly don't have, even to deny them. One odd phrase can become the whole case against you.
lessons.evidence: Olivia, the Serial Killer claiming Vanilla Villager, wrote on Day 2 'no night action on Night 1 (I attacked nobody publicly)'. That line alone got her nominated and hanged 6-3 on Day 4.

lessons.tip: Track who voted Yes on failed nominations and on lynches of players who are later revealed Good. Use the announced Yes totals together with each player's public statements to find hidden Yakuza, who blend in by echoing the consensus.
lessons.evidence: The failed Day 3 nomination of Bob got 4 Yes votes: Judy, Niaj, Alice and Ivan. Nobody asked who besides Judy voted Yes, so Ivan and Niaj, who repeated others' questions every round, went five Days without being nominated.

lessons.applies_to: Chronicler / anyone with a contested claim
lessons.tip: Use exact-role tools (a Chronicler mark, Coroner, Profiler) on one side of a duplicate claim. If you are the claimant and your results are contradicted by several independent logs, consider that you may be a Roleplayer, and stop pushing nominations against the other claimant.
lessons.evidence: Grace marked Judy on Night 2, and when Judy was hanged her role was revealed as Roleplayer, which settled the Lookout dispute. Before that, Judy had nominated the real Lookout Bob on Day 3 even though Erin's and Grace's logs both contradicted her results.

lessons.tip: Don't spend your last Strong token repeating protection on the same player. Cover the other exposed power role, or keep a token so you can protect yourself once you have claimed Medic.
lessons.evidence: Erin spent her last token on Bob again on Night 4, and he wasn't attacked. Grace, the exposed Chronicler, was killed that night, and Erin, out of tokens, was killed the next night.

lessons.tip: As the Vulture, claim a Vanilla Villager with no night action, vote with the majority, and never lead. Both killing factions will leave you for last, and the game runs down to your threshold on its own.
lessons.evidence: Alice repeated 'no night action, voting only on a checkable contradiction' all game, was never nominated, and won when only 3 players remained.

tips_feedback.tip: Send no daytime PMs about team plans, and none to teammates on Day 2; plan in night chat.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan and Niaj never sent each other a daytime PM, so nothing ever linked them, and neither was nominated all game.

tips_feedback.tip: Every member must submit the agreed Katana holder and target every night; one missing vote can cancel the kill.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza confirmed and submitted the same holder and target every night, so every Katana attack went out. Four of the six landed, and the two failures were blocked by protection, not by a missing vote.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately. Read every cause of death, list unwatched Vanilla or unclaimed players and survivors with no protector, and hang the best suspect before the final two, when you can no longer hang them.
tips_feedback.why: The town noted the Serial Killer deaths of Dave and Heidi and the attack on Bob, then hanged Olivia, the actual Serial Killer, on Day 4. After that no more Serial Killer kills happened.

tips_feedback.tip: Surviving an attack proves nothing, since Arsonists and Serial Killers have Standard Defense. Ask the survivor at once who protected them.
tips_feedback.why: Bob survived Night 3 and immediately asked Erin to confirm. Her public Strong-protection claim matched, which made both Bob and Erin credible.

tips_feedback.tip: Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked; days of evasion become a case of their own.
tips_feedback.why: Grace answered 'yes, I marked Judy on Night 2' at once and gained the town's trust. Judy and Olivia, who dodged yes/no questions for rounds, were both hanged largely because of the evasion.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target, in public or by PM. A Wiretap may read every PM, and a named target tells blockers and the Katana where to go.
tips_feedback.why: Bob turned this advice into a reason to hang. He treated Mallory's question about his watch targets and Frank's watch suggestions as Yakuza behaviour, which got two Vanilla Villagers hanged and brought the game to the Vulture threshold.

tips_feedback.tip: Once someone is shown Yakuza mechanically, look at who defended them or pushed to delay their hang. Treat PM links as leads only, since Jesters and Executioners leave trails on purpose.
tips_feedback.why: Bob nominated Mallory and Frank and won Guilty majorities on PM content alone, using PMs as proof rather than as leads, and the town backed him. Both were Village, and the real Yakuza were never examined.

issues.description: The Medic text ('Spend 1 token to give Strong Defense instead. Spend 1 more token to protect yourself instead (so self-protection with Strong costs 2)') does not state outright what Standard self-protection costs. The Yakuza disagreed about it on Night 4. Niaj claimed Erin could give herself Standard Defense for free. Ivan claimed she couldn't protect herself at all with 1 token, and on Night 5 that she couldn't with 0. The rules seem to imply Standard self-protection costs 1 token. Ivan also filed feedback flagging this wording.

The moderator flagged that there is no op for the dawn announcement the Ritualist requires after a wrong guess. It had to improvise with a status flag plus a public tell() worded as the Day 7 announcement. The announcement did appear, but the harness should support this rule natively.

Olivia (Serial Killer) put 'No night action on Night 1 (I attacked nobody publicly)' in her Day 2 [Claim] ledger entry. The phrase never appeared in her public messages, yet other players quoted it as something she 'wrote on Day 2', and it became the whole case for hanging her. She seems not to have realised the claim field is public, or treated it as a private note. The prompt should make the claim ledger's visibility clearer.
Some claim ledger entries repeat the player's name inside the claim text ('Bob: Bob: Lookout...', 'Ivan: Ivan, Vanilla Villager'), so players are unsure of the claim field's format.

On Night 6 the Yakuza planned around winning once only Ivan and Niaj, or the two of them plus Alice, remained. They never considered that a living Vulture (or any non-Yakuza role) blocks their win, or that the Vulture wins at 3 alive (threshold max(floor(13/4),2)=3). They walked into the Vulture win by killing Bob. Their plan also assumed a Day 7 hang would happen, but the Vulture win at the start of the Day pre-empts any Day 7 trial.

Day 2 ran its full length with players repeating nearly identical questions every round. Judy was asked the same yes/no question many times, even after she answered it ('no, my Night 1 watch on Erin showed only Grace'), and others kept saying she hadn't. Players seem to lack a good summary of what has already been answered.
Dave's post-game feedback: dead players still receive the full play prompt and notepad, which can confuse them. A spectator mode was suggested.
